comment: The non-transactional criterion is doing two different jobs and risks misclassification. It usefully excludes point-of-care workflow engines, but read literally it would also exclude a consent or authorisation service, which processes very high real-time transaction volumes while being unambiguously infrastructural. The intended distinction appears to concern the nature of the function rather than the volume of calls.

public.text: The non-transactional criterion is doing two different jobs and risks misclassification. It usefully excludes point-of-care workflow engines, but read literally it would also exclude a consent or authorisation service, which processes very high real-time transaction volumes while being unambiguously infrastructural. The intended distinction appears to concern the nature of the function rather than the volume of calls.
public.suggestedRevision: Reword to separate clinical or administrative transaction processing from high-volume infrastructural operation. Suggested wording: 'not a processor of clinical or administrative transactions within a care or business workflow, though it may operate at high transaction volume in performing infrastructural functions such as identity resolution, authorisation or localisation'.
